variant: remote control for Cat crawler dozers and excavators
name: Cat Command remote control for dozers and excavators
summary: Caterpillar's remote control system for its crawler dozers and excavators: control commands go over the internet or a VPN straight to the machine electronics, so an operator can drive and dig from a station far away or without line of sight. Sold in Germany by the Cat dealer Zeppelin and used there for explosive ordnance clearance.

germany.statusNote: Offered by Zeppelin, the Cat dealer in Germany; the German ordnance clearance firm Eggers Kampfmittelbergung bought its Cat Command system through Zeppelin and runs a Cat D5 dozer with it. No price published; ask the dealer. Caterpillar's own Cat Command pages could not be read (robots.txt unavailable).

sellers.name: Zeppelin Baumaschinen (Cat dealer Germany)
sellers.note: Named by the German customer Eggers as the local Cat dealer 'who offers Cat Command'; showed Cat Command at bauma. Price on request.

specs.label: Control link
specs.value: operator station like a machine cab; commands sent over the internet and VPN to the machine electronics in real time
specs.quote: The preliminary stage to the autonomous construction machine described is based on remote control based on a machine-like operator station by transmission of the control commands via the Internet and VPN.

specs.label: Longest demo distance
specs.conditions: Cat 320 excavator and D5 dozer at Tucson, Arizona, controlled from bauma in Munich
specs.quote: The distance is even greater at 9,419 kilometers when a Cat crawler excavator 320 and Cat crawler dozer D5 are moved in the Caterpillar Mining Center in Tucson, Arizona.

specs.label: Machines shown
specs.value: Cat 340 and 320 crawler excavators, D7 and D5 crawler dozers
specs.quote: direct control of a Cat crawler excavator 340 or crawler dozer D7 some 2,368 kilometers away at the Caterpillar Demonstration and Learning Center in Málaga, Spain – and that without direct line of sight using only monitors

notes: Remote control, not autonomy: a human operator drives the machine from a console or remote station.
Capabilities describe tracked host machines (Cat crawler excavators and dozers); dozers have a blade, not an arm.
Named use cases: remote work in dangerous places such as explosive ordnance clearance or nuclear power plant dismantling (HeavyQuipMag on Zeppelin's bauma show).
